name: Top-Down Memoization
summary: Recursively ask 'fewest coins for this amount?', trying each coin as the last one used, and cache every sub-amount's answer in a memo array so it is solved only once.
visualizationIntent: init: show a memo array of length amount+1, all set to a sentinel (unsolved) except memo[0]=0. recurse: the amt pointer marks the sub-amount being solved; the call-stack panel shows the recursion depth. check: on a memoized cell, reuse it instead of recomputing. update: after trying every coin, store the minimum in memo[amt] and turn the cell green. return: memo[amount] holds the answer, or -1 if it stays at the sentinel.

lineExplanations.3: Pick a sentinel 'infinity' (amount+1) that means an amount is not solvable / not yet solved.
lineExplanations.4: Create the memo array, one slot per amount from 0 to amount, all starting at the sentinel.
lineExplanations.5: The base case: zero coins are needed to make amount 0.
lineExplanations.6: Kick off the recursion for the full target amount.
lineExplanations.7: If the answer never dropped below the sentinel, the amount is impossible.
lineExplanations.9: Return the minimum number of coins (or -1).
lineExplanations.12: Base case inside the recursion: amount 0 needs 0 coins.
lineExplanations.14: If this sub-amount was already solved, reuse the cached answer.
lineExplanations.15: Return the memoized result without recomputing.
lineExplanations.16: Start the best-for-this-amount at the sentinel (unknown).
lineExplanations.17: Try each coin as the last coin used.
lineExplanations.18: Only a coin no larger than the remaining amount can be used.
lineExplanations.19: Recurse on the smaller amount left after taking this coin.
lineExplanations.20: Using this coin costs one more coin than solving the remainder.
lineExplanations.21: Keep this candidate only if it beats the best found so far.
lineExplanations.22: Record the new best coin count for this amount.
lineExplanations.23: Cache the finished answer for this amount so it is never recomputed.
lineExplanations.24: Return the minimum coins for this amount.

syntaxExplanations.1: class Solution: defines the class wrapper expected by the platform.
syntaxExplanations.2: def coinChange(self, coins, amount): receives the coin denominations and the target amount.
syntaxExplanations.3: inf = amount + 1 is a value larger than any real coin count, used as 'infinity'.
syntaxExplanations.4: memo = [inf] * (amount + 1) makes amount+1 slots, all initialized to the sentinel.
syntaxExplanations.5: memo[0] = 0 records the base case directly in the table.
syntaxExplanations.6: best = self.solve(coins, amount, memo, inf) starts the recursive search.
syntaxExplanations.7: if best >= inf: is true when no combination of coins reached the amount.
syntaxExplanations.8: best = -1 signals that the amount cannot be formed.
syntaxExplanations.9: return best sends back the minimum coin count or -1.
syntaxExplanations.11: def solve(self, coins, amt, memo, inf): solves one sub-amount amt, sharing the memo.
syntaxExplanations.12: if amt == 0: is the recursion's base case.
syntaxExplanations.13: return 0 because no coins are needed for amount 0.
syntaxExplanations.14: if memo[amt] != inf: is true when this amount was already solved.
syntaxExplanations.15: return memo[amt] reuses the cached answer.
syntaxExplanations.16: best = inf starts this amount's answer as 'unknown'.
syntaxExplanations.17: for c in coins: tries every coin denomination.
syntaxExplanations.18: if c <= amt: skips coins that are too large to use here.
syntaxExplanations.19: sub = self.solve(coins, amt - c, memo, inf) solves the remaining amount.
syntaxExplanations.20: cand = sub + 1 adds the coin just used to the remainder's count.
syntaxExplanations.21: if cand < best: keeps the smaller coin count.
syntaxExplanations.22: best = cand updates the best answer for this amount.
syntaxExplanations.23: memo[amt] = best caches the finished result.
syntaxExplanations.24: return best hands this amount's answer back to the caller.
